responsibilities.label: Morning briefing
responsibilities.prompt: Prepare my morning briefing from my selected connected accounts: today's agenda, priority messages, deadlines and outstanding follow-ups. State unavailable sources. Do not change source systems unless my policy and standing instructions authorize it.

responsibilities.label: Priority alerts
responsibilities.prompt: Connection health for all selected apps is checked by the platform and connection warnings are delivered separately; do not duplicate them. If no email app is selected, return FLOASSIST_NO_UPDATE after reading preferences. Check my selected email accounts for newly important messages since the last successful check. Apply my priority contacts, quiet hours and interruption preferences. Notify only on meaningful new information; do not repeat previous alerts.

responsibilities.label: Calendar conflicts
responsibilities.prompt: Check for new or changed conflicts across my selected calendars. Propose resolutions; apply changes only under my effective Flolah policy and standing instructions. Do not repeat unchanged conflicts.

responsibilities.label: Deadline tracking
responsibilities.prompt: Check my selected email and file sources for new, revised or resolved deadlines. For email, first list recent messages newest-first using a broad date window (last 7 days), without subject, importance, unread or deadline-keyword filters. Inspect the actual message body for every message in that bounded result before deciding whether it contains a commitment; a subject-only result is discovery, not evidence that no deadline exists. Use floassist_source_read with the exact returned thread/source ID and follow its bounded content pages. Review current thread progression so superseded messages do not create stale commitments. Review up to 40 messages per selected mailbox, follow pagination within that budget, and explicitly report partial coverage if more remain or any body cannot be read. Never select only familiar threads from a previous check. Extract submission, approval, payment, renewal and reply commitments expressed as dates or relative times, even when neither subject nor body contains the words deadline or due. Keyword searches may supplement this pass but must not replace it. For each verified actionable deadline, include the requested action, source subject/reference, exact local date/time and timezone. Distinguish a task for me from an informational date. Read selected file sources when applicable and state any unreviewed sources. Ask about ambiguous dates before creating commitments. Do not create reminders or change source systems merely to report a deadline. Report meaningful findings; return FLOASSIST_NO_UPDATE only when the bounded scan completed with no actionable findings. Do not claim complete coverage after a truncated, failed or subject-only scan.

responsibilities.label: Follow-up tracking
responsibilities.prompt: Check selected mailboxes for unanswered sent requests and explicitly tracked threads. Use discovery tools to list current sent threads, then floassist_source_read for the exact source bodies in this run; existing Kanban tasks alone are not a mailbox check. Inspect up to 40 sent messages from the last 7 days, paginate within that budget and read relevant thread bodies/replies. Identify requests with an explicit reply deadline that has passed or an owner-configured follow-up interval; do not invent urgency for an undated message. Include previously tracked obligations by exact source identity. Report incomplete coverage or connector failures instead of claiming completion. An event invitation or a deadline to submit work is not automatically an unanswered sent request. For qualifying obligations, call floassist_tracking_observe with the current scheduled_goal_id and run_key; do not call track, acknowledge, stop or snooze unless the user explicitly requested that state change. Close only verified resolved sources under the tracking provenance rules; ask if ambiguous. Notify the owner through the task alert queue, and do not send email to recipients unless the effective policy and standing instructions authorize it.
